primary_task: Run an nf-core pipeline (rnaseq, sarek or atacseq) on local FASTQ files: environment check, test profile, samplesheet, run with -profile docker, verify outputs.

requirements.name: docker
requirements.evidence: Step 1: Environment Check (MUST pass) ... Do not proceed until all checks pass; Step 3 'nextflow run nf-core/<pipeline> -r <version> -profile test,docker'; Step 5c '-profile docker'
requirements.basis: a Docker daemon (docker, docker compose and container builds cannot run)

requirements.name: nextflow >= 23.04
requirements.evidence: Not installed | `curl -s https://get.nextflow.io | bash && mv nextflow ~/bin/`
requirements.basis: GitHub release downloads are open (nextflow releases are on github.com), although get.nextflow.io itself is not on the allow-list

requirements.name: nf-core pipeline and container registries (quay.io / docker hub, iGenomes S3)
requirements.basis: Pipelines come from github.com (open); container registries and iGenomes hosts are not listed, so 'other hosts are refused' would apply; would need to check

requirements.name: NCBI GEO/SRA
requirements.evidence: Step 0: Acquire Data (GEO/SRA Only). Skip this step if user has local FASTQ files.
requirements.basis: only PyPI, npm, GitHub, Ubuntu apt archives, NuGet and the Go module proxy are open; other hosts are refused

requirements.name: 8 CPUs / 32 GB memory
requirements.basis: Manifest gives no CPU or memory sizing

notes: The doc mentions singularity only as '(or `singularity` for HPC)' and the environment check's critical items are Docker-based, so I treated Docker as hard. Under a reading where singularity or conda is an acceptable alternative, the verdict would turn on whether those can run (unknown) and containers can be pulled (registries probably refused).
